gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Retro screen glow: Visitor pulls strokes like solder through a nozzle, while Noto Sans Old Italic keeps caps close to x-height. Old-school and modern sit together, one nostalgic, the other crisp and contemporary.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-old-pers: Visitor sets a nostalgic, digital tone, its lowercase a drawn without any thin hairlines and its ascenders kept short. Noto Sans Old Persian lets text run on comfortably, its lofty lowercase opening into the white space.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-psalter-: Nostalgic to the core, Visitor never thins its curves at the turns, like solder squeezed from a nozzle. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, its capitals barely rising, adds a professional, approachable counterweight.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Visitor has the look of an old digital display, its lines uniform with no thick-thin flicker. And Noto Sans Syriac adds tall lowercase like blown glass bulbs, so the page feels warm rather than stiff.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-syriac-w: Constant-width outlines you could trace with a finger give Visitor its nostalgic, digital look. Noto Sans Syriac Western, plain sans and modern, holds its terminals far from the stroke body.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Nostalgic by nature, Visitor puts on a display of constant-width pen lines and big bowls. Noto Sans Tangsa is the one built for easy reading, with wide round openings and short ascender stems.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-tc: Retro and digital: Visitor holds its joins as slim as a pipe cleaner, and its e opens wide. And Noto Sans TC lets long text flow, with large open counters and curves that open outward.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads crisp and professional, its high-set midline and connected counters keeping letters open to the outside. Visitor, meanwhile, is the showpiece, tracing nostalgic digital shapes in one thickness.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Visitor looks nostalgic and digital, its outline plain and unmodulated. Noto Sans Wancho comes in hulking and chalky, its e left wide at the terminal, so the two feel weighty together.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-warang-c: Horizontals and verticals of identical thickness, like rod stock, give Visitor a nostalgic, digital look all its own. Noto Sans Warang Citi forms solid word blocks, with wide channels into counters.
